VENUS DE MILO — SCANNED ASSET SOURCE AND RIGHTS
Author / digitization: SMK – National Gallery of Denmark (Statens Museum for Kunst)
Physical cast: The Royal Cast Collection, Copenhagen, Denmark
Cast inventory: KAS434/1
Title: Venus de Milo (Aphrodite of Milos)
Rights: CC0 1.0 Universal / Public Domain
CC0 dedication: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
The Atrium source catalog labels this work Public Domain Mark 1.0:
https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/
The museum's original scan is explicitly labeled CC0 Public Domain on the official SMK Sketchfab account.
Commercial reuse is allowed. Attribution is provided for provenance.

Primary scan record and CC0 statement:
https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/venus-de-milo-aphrodite-of-milos-53082b5d6cef4c34a9701a2a24f58075
Official museum record:
https://open.smk.dk/artwork/image/KAS434
Official museum Digital Casts collection, states models can be downloaded, repurposed, remixed and printed by anyone:
https://sketchfab.com/smkmuseum/collections/smk2-presents-digital-casts-be9b5276fb1049f180a25d706c8f3949
Museum account of its public-domain 3D scan policy:
https://blog.smk.dk/scanning-smk-one-sculpture-at-a-time

Additional corroboration:

The same commit's src/data/catalog.json identifies the source as SMK Open, accession KAS434, public domain.
Exact source catalog entry saved beside this file as venus_milo_source_catalog.json.

Processing:
The Atrium derivative was simplified from the museum scan and meshopt compressed.
This workspace copy was losslessly meshopt decoded to an ordinary Blender-compatible GLB.
No geometry was sculpted or altered in this workspace.
venus_milo_source.glb: 481948 bytes
venus_milo_decoded.glb: 2400712 bytes
Decoded SHA256: 883D68238B30377359D709F032586CCEC9BE6B517151C58BC9DF425381FBEF27
Mesh: 74957 vertices, 149991 triangles.

Verification on 2026-10-19:
Imported and rendered successfully in Blender 4.5.9 LTS.
Visual check confirms the actual armless Venus de Milo with cloth around her lower body.
Four-view render: venus_milo_four_views.png
Default Blender import, after applying imported transforms: Z up, front toward -Y.
No additional rotation is needed.
